Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Reno NV
219 AM PST Wed Nov 25 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

* Outside of a few light showers in northeast CA early this  
  morning, dry and warmer weather prevails for much of the 
  Thanksgiving holiday period through Saturday.

* Patchy freezing fog returns each morning Thanksgiving Day and
  Friday around fog prone valleys of eastern CA including I-80 
  near Truckee, otherwise expect favorable travel conditions.

* The next storm brings rain and higher elevation snow Sunday into 
  Monday, followed by a potentially stronger storm as December 
  begins, bringing a return of travel impacts in the Sierra. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...

A weakening Pacific storm is moving across CA with a rain area 
from the SF Bay area to the I-5 corridor falling apart as it 
approaches the Sierra. While a few sprinkles or higher elevation 
snow flurries can't be ruled out through mid-morning north of I-80 
in northeast CA, chances for measurable precip up to 0.05" are 
only about 20% in far western Lassen County and less than 10% 
across the rest of northeast CA. Elsewhere, a thick mid-high level  
cloud deck will exit to the east today, allowing for a slight
warmup this afternoon with highs ranging from the upper 40s-mid 
50s. 

For tonight through Saturday, a ridge of high pressure will keep
mainly dry conditions in place, although periods of cirrus will 
be present each day as a weak trough passage flattens the ridge
across northern CA-NV. A few guidance scenarios still indicate a
low end (15-25%) chance for light rain showers north of
Susanville-Gerlach to the OR border around Friday night. Overall,
expect favorable travel conditions across the Sierra and western 
NV, other than patchy freezing fog each morning before 9 AM along 
I-80 near Truckee/Martis Valley. Light winds will lead to valley 
inversions each morning through Saturday, but afternoons will warm 
up to above late November averages, with highs mainly in the 50s 
to near 60 for lower elevations and Sierra communities. 
 
From Sunday through much of next week, a more active storm pattern 
is poised to return. The first chance for rain and higher 
elevation snow along with breezy-gusty winds is targeting the 
Sunday-Monday time frame, with highest probabilities (50-90% for 
the Sierra/northeast CA and 20-60% for western NV) favoring Sunday
afternoon-evening. This system looks to remain on the warmer side
with snow levels near or above 7000-7500 feet. Snow could still 
affect higher open mountain passes in the Sierra, so anyone 
traveling as the holiday weekend wraps up should allow extra time,  
even if roads are just wet or slushy at pass level.

As we get into the first few days of December, additional storms
are lining up to reach the western US. Ensemble guidance is still
varied on timing and how much precipitation will fall, but the 
trend still favors increased impacts compared to the Sunday-Monday  
storm. Snow levels most likely range from 5500-6500 ft, but some 
colder scenarios with a period of 4500-5000 ft snow levels are 
also in the mix. Overall, plan for winter conditions if planning 
travel across the Sierra next week. 

MJD

&&

.AVIATION...

KRNO Forecast: 

* VFR conditions with light surface winds prevail into early 
  Thursday AM. The thicker cloud deck exits to the east later this
  morning, with areas of cirrus returning tonight. 

Regional Outlook: 

* For KTRK, thick cloud cover and drier surface conditions will
  limit FZFG formation this morning, but clearing this afternoon
  and a thinner cirrus deck should allow for FZFG to return late
  tonight and early Thursday AM, mainly after 08Z. Otherwise, VFR
  conditions with light surface winds prevail with decreasing mid- 
  high clouds today and areas of cirrus returning tonight (similar
  to KRNO). Lingering S-SW FL100 winds up to 35 kt diminish after
  15Z this morning, ending any LLWS and reducing turbulence. 
  
24-72 Hour Outlook: 

* VFR conditions with light winds continue through early Saturday,
  except for FZFG potential (60-80% chance) with LIFR conditions
  each morning at KTRK. However, areas of cirrus may limit the
  duration and extent of this fog. Valley inversions may also lead
  to increased haze buildup mainly around KRNO/KCXP/KMEV each
  morning, with minor reductions in slantwise visibility.

MJD
